title: Stephen Vaughn on the U.S.-China Disconnect - The Wire China
gist: Paywalled Q&A teaser with trade lawyer Stephen Vaughn (King & Spalding, former USTR general counsel in the first Trump administration) on the U.S.-China disconnect; only his bio and Hamiltonian industrial-policy framing are visible.

insights.claim: Stephen Vaughn, former USTR general counsel, is an ardent supporter of manufacturers and industrial policy, framing it in the tradition of Alexander Hamilton's 1791 Report on Manufactures.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The Hamiltonian framing signals that tariff-backed industrial policy is viewed as a durable American tradition, not a temporary deviation.
insights.quote: Politico called Stephen Vaughn “the Hamiltonian at USTR” because of his ardent support for manufacturers and industrial policy

insights.claim: In the first Trump administration Vaughn helped develop the USTR trade case that led to heavy tariffs on China, making him an architect of the current tariff regime.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Views from architects of the Section-301-style tariffs are a leading indicator of hawkish trade-policy direction.
